title: Lightweight request lineage beacon and hybrid hop-mapper for SDKs
creator: Marina Chen
description: Goal: implement a compact, low-overhead "request lineage beacon" and accompanying SDK middleware (injectors/extractors) to reliably reconstruct end-to-end call graphs across heterogeneous transports (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSockets, SSE, gRPC, worker queues). This work targets high-QPS production paths where adding full baggage or large headers is too expensive, and where partial/streamed responses (chunked bodies, SSE) and async worker handoffs currently break lineage linking.
background: Existing approaches rely on full OpenTelemetry baggage or long multi-field headers which increase request size and cause fragmentation for mobile and edge clients. We also see lost ancestry when requests go over WebSocket bridges, chunked responses, or are enqueued to background workers. There is prior infra (ENG-61234 request-fabric-edge-observability-proxy) and several propagation shims; this ticket consolidates a production-friendly, forward-compatible lineage header + SDK hooks and rollout plan.
design_decisions: Use a single compact header (X-RW-Lineage) with a v1+base64 compact TLV payload to minimize header count and enable forward extensibility
Keep cryptographic operations optional; support an HMAC flag for high-security customers but default to unsigned compact IDs to reduce CPU on hot paths
Format: v1|<64bit_span_id>|<parent_hash>|<sampling_hint>|<flags> encoded in base64 to keep header length < 48 bytes in typical cases
Provide SDK middleware for Node/Python/Go that does non-blocking injection and best-effort extraction; fall back to mapping from traceparent/w3c headers where lineage header is absent
Expose a lightweight runtime API to stitch lineage when worker queues/async handoffs occur (sequence token + optional attached span snapshot), stored in the request metadata store for 24h by default
Avoid adding to existing baggage fields to prevent baggage explosion; map lineage to OpenTelemetry trace/span fields when exporting to backend
acceptance_criteria: Header format documented in design doc and Confluence (link included) and accepted by tracing team
Node/Python/Go SDK middleware implemented and published to internal packages with examples
End-to-end tests that demonstrate lineage preservation across HTTP->WebSocket->worker->HTTP flows
Microbenchmarks show median injection overhead < 0.05ms on a cold Node baseline and < 0.02ms on warm runtimes
At least one customer staging workload validates lineage reconstruction for chunked responses and SSE without increasing payload size by >3%
Console dashboards updated: new 'lineage loss' metric, and a call-graph view showing stitched hops for sampled traces
Migration plan and fallback strategy documented: how to handle clients that strip headers and how to progressively enable HMAC for enterprise customers
tasks: Spike: implement minimal header encoder/decoder and run microbenchmarks (Node/Python) — done
Implement Node SDK middleware (non-blocking header injection + extraction) and unit tests
Implement Python and Go SDK equivalents and integration tests
Add server-side stitcher logic for worker enqueue/dequeue events and sequence token storage
Create end-to-end integration harness (HTTP -> WS proxy -> worker -> HTTP) and CI job
Update Console to consume new lineage field and add lineage-loss/time-to-stitch dashboards
Run customer-stage trial with 2 customers, collect telemetry, and tune sampling_hint defaults
Write rollout runbook: feature flags, opt-in per-tenant, HMAC enablement steps
notes: We must coordinate with the Console team to ensure high-cardinality fields are not surfaced by default. For enterprise customers requiring non-repudiation we will enable HMAC signing; downside is CPU cost — provide benchmarking data and an opt-in knob.
